title: Bellarmino rejects Thomas here: Saint-vows aim to honor Saints, and some formulas vow to God and Saints together
source_text: XXIX. Verum haec solutio Bellarmino non satisfacit: quoniam ita Thomae observatio recte quidem applicari potest ad vota quae includunt promissionem homini mortali factam. Nam qui vovet, verbi causa, obedientiam Praelato, revera votum non Praelato, sed Deo soli facit, licet ipsi Praelato obedientiam promittat. Nec enim illo voto Praelatum, sed Deum colere & honorare intendit. At qui vovet jejunium vel peregrinationem Sanctis intendit ipsos Sanctos religiose honorare. Adde quod fiunt Sanctis quaedam promissiones quas apparet non solum esse materiam voti sed votum quoddam formaliter. Ut quum quis se addicturus ordini Religioso, votum hac forma concipit, Voveo Deo, & Beatae Mariae, & omnibus Sanctis, me Praelato tali vel tali obediturum. Ibi enim sola promissio Praelato facta est materia voti, altera vero quae ad Deum & Sanctos simul dirigitur, est formaliter ipsum votum.
pass_a_gloss: But this solution does not satisfy Bellarmine: because thus Thomas’s observation can indeed be rightly applied to vows which include a promise made to a mortal man. For he who vows, for example, obedience to a Prelate, in reality makes the vow not to the Prelate but to God alone, although he promises obedience to the Prelate himself. For by that vow he intends to cultivate and honor not the Prelate, but God. But he who vows a fast or pilgrimage to the Saints intends to honor the Saints themselves religiously. Add that certain promises are made to the Saints which appear to be not only the matter of a vow but a vow formally. As when someone about to bind himself to a Religious order conceives a vow in this form: I vow to God, and to Blessed Mary, and to all the Saints, that I will obey such or such a Prelate. For there the promise alone made to the Prelate is the matter of the vow, but the other which is directed to God and the Saints together is formally the vow itself.
pass_b_english: Bellarmino: Thomas fits prelate-obedience vows, not Saint-directed fasts and pilgrimages that mean to honor Saints.
Some formulas vow to God and Mary and all Saints at once—so the Saint-clause is inside the formal vow.

lemmas.gloss: I vow to God and to Blessed Mary

choices.why: Joint God-and-Saints direction inside the vow form.
